# Phone check script and docs

## What to build

The phone work for graph-manager is already in the codebase (see "What earlier work delivered" below). This slice adds the checks and the docs. (1) A new end-to-end script `apps/graph-manager/scripts/ui-mobile.sh`, built like the existing `ui-smoke.sh`: a fake forge, graph-manager on free ports, `--provider fake` runs and agent-browser. At 390 × 844 and at 360 × 740 it asserts that no page scrolls sideways on Login, Runs, a finished run, a live run (and inside its iframe), Terminals, Workspaces, Projects, Reviewers and Settings. It checks that the phone top bar shows (but not on Login), opens and closes the nav drawer, and on Terminals opens a shell, taps the terminal, checks that xterm's textarea has focus and the extra-keys row shows, and uses the extra keys to type into the real shell. (2) An npm script `ui:mobile` in `apps/graph-manager/package.json`, which is not part of `npm test`. (3) A wiki page `docs/wiki/features/mobile-web.md` with the decision table, the known follow-ups, the code references and a manual checklist for a real iPhone and a real Android phone, linked from `docs/wiki/index.md`. (4) An "On a phone" note in `apps/graph-manager/README.md`. Do not change any source file under `src/`. If the script finds a real bug in the earlier work, fix it in the smallest way and say so in your summary.

### What earlier work delivered (in the codebase now — verify with grep before relying on it)

- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/ui/media.ts`: `NARROW = "(max-width: 899.98px)"`, `PHONE = "(max-width: 599.98px)"`, `COARSE = "(pointer: coarse)"`, `useMedia(query)`. It uses `window.matchMedia` with a `change` listener.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/ui/viewport.ts`: `useVisualViewport()`, called in `Shell.tsx`. It sets `--app-h` on `<html>` and toggles the class `kb-open` on `<html>` (`html.kb-open`) while the phone keyboard is open. It also exports `isKeyboardOpen()`.
- `Shell.tsx` / `Shell.css`: below 900 px there is a `<header className="gm-topbar" data-testid="gm-topbar">`. It holds the menu button `data-testid="nav-menu"` (`aria-label="Open navigation"`, `aria-expanded`), the brand and the page title. ☰ opens the nav as `.gm-nav.drawer` (fixed on the left, `width: min(300px, 86vw)`) over a scrim `.gm-nav-scrim` with `data-testid="nav-scrim"`. A nav link tap (route change), a scrim tap or Escape closes it. `html.kb-open` hides `.gm-topbar` below 900 px.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/components/touch.ts`: `attachTouch(host, term, { onTap })` on the `.terminal-view` element (`data-testid="terminal-view-<id>"`). It only handles `pointerType === "touch"`. A `pointerup` that moved less than 10 px calls `term.focus()` and then `onTap()`. A vertical move of 10 px or more is a swipe that sends `WheelEvent`s to `term.element`.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/components/ExtraKeys.tsx`: `<div className="extra-keys" role="toolbar" aria-label="Terminal keys" data-testid="extra-keys">` with the buttons `xk-esc`, `xk-tab`, `xk-ctrl` (`aria-pressed`), `xk-up`, `xk-down`, `xk-left`, `xk-right` and `xk-prefix` (label `Ctrl Space`, shown as `⌃␣`). Each button calls `preventDefault()` on `pointerdown` and acts on `click`. They send `\x1b`, `\t`, and `\x1b[A`/`[B`/`[D`/`[C` (or `\x1bOA`… in application cursor mode). Ctrl is sticky for one key, and `xk-prefix` arms the `Ctrl Space` prefix. `Terminals.tsx` renders it at the bottom of `.terms-main` only when `useMedia(COARSE)` is true and a terminal on the page has focus.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/public/manifest.webmanifest` (served at `/manifest.webmanifest` as `application/manifest+json`, no login needed), `public/sw.js` (served at `/sw.js` with `Cache-Control: no-cache`; on a failed navigation it answers a page titled "graph-manager is not reachable" with a **Retry** button), `public/icons/` (`apple-touch-icon.png`, `icon-192.png`, `icon-512.png`, `icon-maskable-512.png`, made by `apps/graph-manager/scripts/make-icons.mjs`), `ui/standalone.ts` (`isStandalone`, `useStandaloneLinks`, `registerSw`), and the **Install app** section in Settings.
- HTTPS: `GM_TLS_CERT`, `GM_TLS_KEY`, `GM_TRUST_PROXY` (`config.ts`), the `--tls-cert`/`--tls-key` flags on `graph-execution manager`, and a `Secure` cookie on HTTPS. The README section **HTTPS setup (phones and installing the app)** (GitHub anchor `#https-setup-phones-and-installing-the-app`) has the Tailscale, own-certificate and Caddy recipes and an **Install on a phone** paragraph.
- The engine's live run page (`packages/graph-execution/src/web/assets`): below 600 px the `#topbar` wraps to two lines and `#phases` scrolls sideways. One finger pans the graph, two fingers pinch-zoom it (`pinchView`, `MIN_K`, `MAX_K` exported from `graph.js`), and a tap on a node opens the panel. `viewport-fit=cover` is set, the panel sheet has safe-area padding, and buttons have 40 px hit areas under `pointer: coarse`.

## Context: files to read before implementing

- `apps/graph-manager/scripts/ui-smoke.sh` (lines 1–156, read all of it). This is the script to mirror: `set -euo pipefail`, `ROOT` and `cd`, `DIR=$(mktemp -d)`, `SESSION`, the `ab()` helper (line 22), `cleanup` with the `web.json` pid kill (24–35), `fail`/`step` (37–44), `free_port` (46), `wait_for` (49–57), `visible` (60), `page_has` (63), `json_get` (65), the builds behind `SKIP_BUILD` (69–73), starting the fake forge and `node apps/graph-manager/dist/server/main.js` with `GM_PASSWORD=pw GM_PORT GM_DATA_DIR GM_WORKSPACES_DIR GM_GITHUB_API_URL` (81–88), the curl login with a cookie jar (89), `ab set viewport 1440 900` (92), the UI login (93–97), and the run start / `applied` wait / view close (122–140).
- `apps/graph-manager/scripts/fake-forge.mjs` (lines 250–275). It seeds `octo/hello` (github) and `grp/sub/proj` (gitlab). The GitHub token is `gh-good` with login `octo`. The CLI is `node fake-forge.mjs <port> <dir>`.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/forges.ts` (lines 46–53): `PUT /api/forges/github {token}`.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/workspaces.ts` (lines 54–57, 170–200): `POST /api/workspaces {forge: "github", fullPath: "octo/hello"}` starts a clone job. Poll until `$DIR/ws/github/octo/hello/.git` exists.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/projects.ts` (lines 32, 85–93): `POST /api/projects {name, workspaces: [id]}`. The name must match letters, digits, `-` and `_`.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/terminals.ts` (lines 12–24, 43–78): `POST /api/terminals {workspaceId}` answers 201 with the terminal info, including `id`. The shell is `$SHELL` (`terminals.ts:124`).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/runs.ts` (line 78): runs get `{ ...process.env, … }`, so `GRAPH_EXECUTION_FAKE_SCRIPT` set on the graph-manager process reaches every fake run. The engine reads the file when a run starts (`packages/graph-execution/src/providers/fake.ts:70-73`), so you can rewrite it between runs.
- `packages/graph-execution/src/providers/fake.ts` (lines 26–45): the attempt fields `write: Record<path, content>`, `hang: true`, `exitCode`. By default an agent writes and commits `<label>.txt`.
- `packages/graph-execution/src/web/server.ts` (lines 220, 336). The engine page has `POST /abort` and `POST /close`, which graph-manager proxies at `$GM/runs/<ws>/<runId>/view/abort` and `…/view/close` (ui-smoke.sh:135 uses `view/close`).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/RunDetail.tsx` (lines 107–115, 369, 399–424): a live run shows `<iframe data-testid="run-live-view">`, and a finished one shows `data-testid="run-static-graph"`. The page is `data-testid="page-run-detail"`.
- Page testids: `page-login`, `page-runs`, `page-terminals`, `page-workspaces`, `page-projects`, `page-reviewers`, `page-settings`, `page-run-detail` (grep `data-testid="page-` under `apps/graph-manager/src/web`).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/Terminals.tsx` (lines 303–309): `/terminals?focus=<id>` opens and focuses that terminal in a pane.
- `apps/graph-manager/package.json` (lines 10–16): the `scripts` block.
- `apps/graph-manager/README.md`: `## The app` (line 257, the nav paragraph says "Below 1100 px … collapses to a 56 px icon rail"), the **Terminals** bullet (it says "Under 900 px the sidebar is a drawer and one pane fills the page"), and `## Local development` (around line 347, where ui-smoke.sh is described).
- `docs/wiki/index.md`: one bullet per feature page under `## Features`.
- `docs/wiki/features/terminal-instant-echo.md`: the format to follow. An intro paragraph, then `## How …`, `## Decisions` (table), `## Known follow-ups`, `## Code` (bullets of `path`: what is there).
- `docs/prd/mobile-web.md`: the approved spec, if it is still at this path (it may have moved to `docs/prd/done/`). Its Decisions table is the source for the wiki table.
- `TESTING.md` "Web view (agent-browser)" (lines 54–77). Look at the result yourself with screenshots.

## Patterns to follow

**Script skeleton (copy from ui-smoke.sh and keep the helpers unchanged):**
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Phone layout check of graph-manager: … Run it from anywhere: bash apps/graph-manager/scripts/ui-mobile.sh
# Needs node, git, curl and agent-browser on the PATH. Not part of `npm test`.
# SKIP_BUILD=1 reuses the existing builds; KEEP=1 keeps the temp dir (its path is printed).
set -euo pipefail
ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../.." && pwd)
cd "$ROOT"
DIR=$(mktemp -d)
SESSION="gm-ui-mobile-$$"
ab() { agent-browser --session "$SESSION" "$@"; }
```

**Touch emulation (checked with agent-browser 0.27.0):**
- `ab set viewport 390 844` sets the width but leaves `matchMedia("(pointer: coarse)").matches` as `false`.
- `ab set device "iPhone 14"` only changes the user agent and the screen size. It does not turn on `pointer: coarse` or touch, so do not rely on it.
- What works is an init script that runs before the app. Pass `--init-script <file>` on the **first** `ab` command of the session (the one that starts the browser, e.g. `ab --init-script "$DIR/coarse.js" open "$GM/login"`). It makes `useMedia(COARSE)` true:
```js
// $DIR/coarse.js: written by the script with a heredoc
(() => {
  const real = window.matchMedia.bind(window);
  window.matchMedia = (q) => /\(\s*pointer\s*:\s*coarse\s*\)/.test(q)
    ? { matches: true, media: q, onchange: null, addEventListener() {}, removeEventListener() {}, addListener() {}, removeListener() {}, dispatchEvent: () => false }
    : real(q);
  Object.defineProperty(navigator, "maxTouchPoints", { get: () => 5 });
})();
```
- This only fools JavaScript. CSS `@media (pointer: coarse)` rules (the 40 px targets, 16 px inputs) still do not apply in headless Chrome, so the script cannot measure them. They are on the manual checklist.

**Overflow assertion, with a useful failure message:**
```bash
no_hscroll() { ab eval 'document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= window.innerWidth' | grep -q true; }
widest() { ab eval '(() => { const w = innerWidth; const bad = [...document.querySelectorAll("body *")].filter((e) => e.getBoundingClientRect().right > w + 1).slice(0, 5).map((e) => e.tagName.toLowerCase() + (e.className && typeof e.className === "string" ? "." + e.className.trim().split(/\s+/).join(".") : "") + " right=" + Math.round(e.getBoundingClientRect().right)); return JSON.stringify({ scrollWidth: document.documentElement.scrollWidth, innerWidth: w, bad }); })()'; }
check_fits() { no_hscroll || fail "$1 scrolls sideways at ${VW}x${VH}: $(widest)"; }
```

## Step-by-step tasks

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/scripts/ui-mobile.sh`

- **IMPLEMENT** (make it executable: `chmod +x`). Use the ui-smoke.sh helpers as they are (`fail`, `step`, `free_port`, `wait_for`, `visible`, `page_has`, `json_get`) and the build step behind `SKIP_BUILD`. Steps in order:
  1. **Setup**: the fake forge on a free port, as in ui-smoke.sh:81–88. Write `$DIR/fake.json` with `{}` first. Start graph-manager with the ui-smoke env plus `GRAPH_EXECUTION_FAKE_SCRIPT="$DIR/fake.json"` and `SHELL="$(command -v bash)"` (a predictable shell with readline, so the arrow keys edit the line). Do the curl API login into `$COOKIE`.
  2. **Login at phone size**: write `$DIR/coarse.js` (above). Run `ab --init-script "$DIR/coarse.js" open about:blank` (this launches the browser with the init script), then `ab set viewport 390 844`, then `ab open "$GM/login"`, then wait for `[data-testid=page-login]`. Run `check_fits Login`. Assert that `gm-topbar` is **not** visible: `! visible '[data-testid=gm-topbar]' || fail …`. Then log in through the UI as ui-smoke.sh:94–97 does (`fill 'input[type=password]' pw`, `press Enter`, wait for `page_has "Start run"`).
  3. **Data through the API** (curl with `-b "$COOKIE"`):
     - `PUT /api/forges/github {"token":"gh-good"}`.
     - `POST /api/workspaces {"forge":"github","fullPath":"octo/hello"}`, then `wait_for 30 … test -d "$CLONE/.git"`.
     - Commit the diamond fixture and `spec.md` as ui-smoke.sh:116–120 does.
     - `POST /api/projects {"name":"mobile","workspaces":["github~octo~hello"]}`.
  4. **Finished run**: `POST /api/runs/$WS {"tasksDir":"diamond","spec":"spec.md","provider":"fake"}`. Wait for `applied` and close its view, as in ui-smoke.sh:129–137. Keep the id in `RUN1`. Then make the tree clean for the next run: `git -C "$CLONE" add -A -- . ':(exclude).graph-execution'` and `git -C "$CLONE" -c user.name=smoke -c user.email=smoke@example.com commit -qm "run 1" || true`.
  5. **Live run**: write `$DIR/fake.json` as `{"task:1":{"attempts":[{"write":{"live/1.txt":"1\n"}}]},"task:2":{"attempts":[{"write":{"live/2.txt":"2\n"}}]},"task:3":{"attempts":[{"hang":true}]}}`. Task 3 then never ends, and the other tasks don't collide with run 1's `<id>.txt` files. Start a second run the same way and keep its id in `RUN2` (a global that `cleanup` uses). Wait until `/api/runs` shows it with `live === true` and status `running`.
  6. **Routes, for each viewport** `390 844` then `360 740` (set `VW`/`VH`, run `ab set viewport $VW $VH`). For each of `/runs` (`page-runs`), `/runs/$WS/$RUN1` (`run-static-graph`), `/runs/$WS/$RUN2` (`run-live-view`), `/terminals` (`page-terminals`), `/workspaces` (`page-workspaces`), `/projects` (`page-projects`), `/reviewers` (`page-reviewers`) and `/settings` (`page-settings`):
     - `ab open "$GM$route"`;
     - `wait_for 15 … visible "[data-testid=<testid>]"`;
     - `check_fits "$route"`;
     - `wait_for 5 "gm-topbar on $route" visible '[data-testid=gm-topbar]'`;
     - assert that `.gm-nav` is not on screen: `ab eval '(() => { const n = document.querySelector(".gm-nav"); if (!n) return true; const r = n.getBoundingClientRect(); return getComputedStyle(n).display === "none" || r.right <= 0 || r.width === 0; })()'` must be `true`.
     - For the live run, also check the iframe. It is on the same origin through graph-manager's proxy. Wait until `document.querySelector("[data-testid=run-live-view]").contentDocument?.querySelector("#topbar")` exists. Then assert that `f.contentDocument.documentElement.scrollWidth <= f.contentWindow.innerWidth`, and that the engine's Abort button `#action` is not `hidden` and has `getBoundingClientRect().right <= f.contentWindow.innerWidth`. Allow up to 15 s for the page to receive state (`#action` starts `hidden`).
  7. **Nav drawer** (at 390 × 844 on `/runs`):
     - `ab click '[data-testid=nav-menu]'`, then wait until `.gm-nav.drawer` and `[data-testid=nav-scrim]` are visible, and assert that `nav-menu` has `aria-expanded="true"` (`ab get attr '[data-testid=nav-menu]' aria-expanded`).
     - **Scrim**: close it with a mouse tap at the right edge, outside the 300 px drawer: `ab mouse move $((VW - 20)) 400; ab mouse down; ab mouse up`. Wait until `.gm-nav.drawer` is gone or hidden.
     - **Escape**: reopen and `ab press Escape`, then the drawer closes.
     - **Nav link**: reopen and `ab click '.gm-nav.drawer a[href="/terminals"]'`. Then the URL ends in `/terminals` (`ab get url`) and the drawer is closed.
  8. **Terminal** (at 390 × 844):
     - `TID=$(curl … -X POST -d '{"workspaceId":"'$WS'"}' "$GM/api/terminals" | json_get 'j.id')`.
     - `ab open "$GM/terminals?focus=$TID"`, then wait until `[data-testid=terminal-view-$TID] .xterm-screen` is visible.
     - Blur first: `ab eval 'document.activeElement && document.activeElement.blur(), true'`. Then tap with synthetic touch pointer events on the terminal host. `attachTouch` only looks at `pointerType`, so synthetic events are enough:
       ```bash
       ab eval '(() => { const h = document.querySelector("[data-testid=terminal-view-'"$TID"'] .xterm-screen"); const r = h.getBoundingClientRect(); const o = { pointerType: "touch", pointerId: 9, isPrimary: true, bubbles: true, cancelable: true, clientX: r.left + 40, clientY: r.top + 40 }; h.dispatchEvent(new PointerEvent("pointerdown", o)); h.dispatchEvent(new PointerEvent("pointerup", o)); return true; })()'
       ```
     - Assert `ab eval 'document.activeElement?.classList.contains("xterm-helper-textarea") === true'` → `true`.
     - Wait until `[data-testid=extra-keys]` is visible, and check that each of `xk-esc xk-tab xk-ctrl xk-up xk-down xk-left xk-right xk-prefix` is visible.
     - **Input reaches the shell**:
       - `ab keyboard type "echo ab"`;
       - `ab click '[data-testid=xk-left]'`;
       - `ab keyboard type "Z"`;
       - `ab click '[data-testid=xk-right]'`;
       - `ab keyboard type " > $DIR/xk.txt"`;
       - `ab press Enter`;
       - `wait_for 10 "the extra keys to edit the line" grep -qx aZb "$DIR/xk.txt"`.
     - **Focus stays**: `ab click '[data-testid=xk-esc]'`, then assert that `document.activeElement` is still the `.xterm-helper-textarea`.
     - **Ctrl toggle**: `ab click '[data-testid=xk-ctrl]'` → `aria-pressed` is `true`. Click it again → `false`.
     - Also run `check_fits /terminals-with-keys` here.
  9. **Desktop is unchanged**: `ab set viewport 1440 900`, `ab open "$GM/runs"`. Then `gm-topbar` is not visible, `.gm-nav` is visible, and `check_fits` still passes.
  10. Print `OK: phone layout checks passed (390x844, 360x740)`.
- **IMPLEMENT** cleanup:
  - Extend ui-smoke's `cleanup` so that, when `RUN2` is set, it first calls `curl -s -b "$COOKIE" -X POST "$GM/runs/$WS/$RUN2/view/abort"`, then polls `/api/runs` for up to 20 s until RUN2 is no longer `running`, then `…/view/close`.
  - After that, do the existing `web.json` pid kills, kill `PIDS`, `ab close`, and `rm -rf "$DIR"` unless `KEEP`.
  - Initialise `RUN2=""` and `GM=""` at the top so `set -u` doesn't trip in `cleanup`.
- **GOTCHA**: `ab click '[data-testid=nav-scrim]'` clicks the centre of the full-screen scrim, and at 390 px the drawer (300 px wide) covers that point, so the click lands on the drawer. Tap the scrim at `x = VW - 20` with `ab mouse`.
- **GOTCHA**: `--init-script` must come on the first command that launches the session's browser. A later `ab --init-script …` on a running session is ignored. `addinitscript` is not a command in 0.27.0.
- **GOTCHA**: terminals render with WebGL, so there is no DOM text to read. Check the shell's effect through a file (`$DIR/xk.txt`), not with `page_has`.
- **GOTCHA**: `ab eval` prints JSON, so `true` prints as `true` and strings come quoted. Use `grep -q true` as `visible`/`page_has` do.
- **GOTCHA**: the second run starts in the same clone, so commit run 1's applied changes first (step 4) or the start may be refused for a dirty tree. If the start still answers an error, print it with `fail "start run 2 answered: $START"`.
- **VALIDATE**: `bash -n apps/graph-manager/scripts/ui-mobile.sh && bash apps/graph-manager/scripts/ui-mobile.sh` ends with `OK: …`. Also take a screenshot at each viewport for at least `/runs` and `/terminals` (`ab screenshot "$DIR/runs-$VW.png"` when `KEEP` is set), then look at them.

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/package.json`

- **IMPLEMENT**: in `scripts`, add `"ui:mobile": "bash scripts/ui-mobile.sh"` after `"start"`. Do not add it to `test`. (`npm run ui:mobile -w graph-manager` runs from `apps/graph-manager`, and the script `cd`s to the repo root itself.)
- **VALIDATE**: `npm run ui:mobile -w graph-manager`.

### CREATE `docs/wiki/features/mobile-web.md`

- **IMPLEMENT** in the format of `docs/wiki/features/terminal-instant-echo.md`:
  - Title `# graph-manager on phones: nav drawer, terminal keyboard and extra keys, PWA, optional HTTPS`.
  - **Intro**: one paragraph. graph-manager's web UI and the engine's live run page work on a 360–430 px phone; it installs as a home-screen app over HTTPS.
  - `## How it works`: short bullets on:
    - the 900 px `NARROW` and 600 px `PHONE` breakpoints, and `pointer: coarse` for touch (`ui/media.ts`);
    - `--app-h` from `visualViewport` and `html.kb-open`;
    - the top bar and drawer;
    - tap-to-focus and swipe-to-scroll (`touch.ts`);
    - the extra-keys row and sticky Ctrl;
    - the PWA manifest, the no-cache service worker and its offline page;
    - HTTPS via `GM_TLS_CERT`/`GM_TLS_KEY` or `GM_TRUST_PROXY`;
    - the engine page's pinch zoom.
  - `## Decisions`: a table with the columns `| Decision | Why | Ticket |`. Ticket is `—` for every row (no Jira ticket yet). Write at least these rows, condensed from the spec's Decisions table:
    1. One narrow breakpoint, `(max-width: 899.98px)`, in `ui/media.ts`.
    2. Touch is `(pointer: coarse)`, not width.
    3. Below 900 px a 48 px top bar with ☰ and a left drawer; the 56 px rail stays for 900–1099 px.
    4. The drawer closes on route change, scrim and Escape, and traps focus.
    5. App height from `visualViewport` (`--app-h`).
    6. The viewport meta has `viewport-fit=cover, interactive-widget=resizes-content` and no `maximum-scale`.
    7. "Keyboard open" = `visualViewport.height < innerHeight - 120` with an editable element focused.
    8. Chrome is hidden while `kb-open` on narrow screens.
    9. A tap is under 10 px of movement and calls `term.focus()` synchronously.
    10. The textarea has autocapitalize/autocorrect off, `enterkeyhint=send` and a 16 px font.
    11. A swipe becomes synthetic `WheelEvent`s.
    12. Extra keys go through `term.input(data, true)`.
    13. The arrows follow application cursor mode.
    14. Ctrl is sticky for one key.
    15. `⌃␣` calls the existing `arm(true)`.
    16. `preventDefault` on `pointerdown` keeps the keyboard open.
    17. The row shows only with `pointer: coarse` and a focused terminal.
    18. Instant echo is off by default on touch.
    19. Tables become cards below 600 px, and the graph and diff scroll in their own box.
    20. Touch targets are 40 px.
    21. The engine page gets its own phone pass (wrap, phase scroll, pinch).
    22. A PWA with no cache and only an offline fallback page.
    23. The service worker only in production, on a secure context.
    24. Committed PNG icons made by `make-icons.mjs`.
    25. Same-origin `target=_blank` links stay in the window when standalone.
    26. `black-translucent` status bar.
    27. HTTPS is optional and off by default; setting only one of cert/key is a startup error.
    28. `GM_TRUST_PROXY` is opt-in.
    29. The cookie is `secure` when `req.protocol === "https"`.
    30. Three README recipes (Tailscale recommended).
    31. The certificate is read once at startup.
    32. Checks are jsdom unit tests plus `ui-mobile.sh` plus a manual phone checklist.
  - `## Known follow-ups`. Include at least:
    - headless agent-browser can't emulate `pointer: coarse` in CSS or a real keyboard, so 40 px targets, `kb-open` and the keyboard refit are only checked by hand;
    - no momentum on terminal swipe;
    - no pinch-to-zoom of the terminal font, and no long-press selection/copy;
    - no Alt/Home/End/PgUp/PgDn extra keys;
    - no hot reload of renewed TLS certificates and no built-in ACME;
    - landscape uses the same rules;
    - add any issue you saw while running the script.
  - `## Manual checklist (real phones)`: two sub-lists, **iPhone (Safari)** and **Android (Chrome)**. Each is a numbered checklist the user ticks, with the expected result for every step:
    1. Open graph-manager over HTTPS (Tailscale `tailscale serve --bg 7420`, then `https://<machine>.<tailnet>.ts.net`, with `GM_TRUST_PROXY=1`). Log in. The cookie is `Secure` (Safari Web Inspector / Chrome remote devtools → Application → Cookies).
    2. ☰ opens the drawer, and a link, the scrim and the edge all close it. Nothing hides under the notch or home bar.
    3. Runs, a finished run, a live run, Workspaces, Projects, Reviewers, Settings: no sideways scroll, and every button is easy to hit.
